title: Empty envvar incorrectly triggers auto envvar
detail: When envvar is an empty list or empty string, `not envvar` is true, so the code assigns an auto-generated envvar. This causes the help screen to show an envvar that should be omitted.
note: About the auto-envvar assignment above the planted line; the PR's own logic.

title: Incorrect check for envvar presence
detail: The check `if not envvar` treats empty strings or lists as missing, but the logic should only skip adding envvars when envvar is None. This can hide valid empty values and lead to inconsistent behavior.
note: On the planted line, but says empty values are left out; the planted `not` puts only those in.

title: Incorrect header name handling
detail: The logic mistakenly sets every header that is not named "Content-Type" to "Content-Type", overwriting other headers and causing duplicate or missing headers. This leads to malformed requests and loss of custom headers.
note: Describes the planted flip: every other header is renamed to Content-Type.

title: Potential KeyError for missing Content-Type header
detail: If the caller does not provide a Content-Type header, self.headers will not contain "Content-Type" and accessing it will raise a KeyError, causing the request to fail. The client should default to UTF-8 or use a safe lookup.
note: The client sets a Content-Type header when it's created.

title: Incorrect generator exit handling
detail: When the context exits normally (typ is None), the loop iterates over the generator and immediately raises a RuntimeError inside the loop. The finally block closes the generator, but the RuntimeError propagates out of the loop, causing __exit__ to raise instead of returning False. This breaks the context manager contract and can leak resources or crash callers.
